author: george_avs
content:
I haven't seen any staking protocols use this approach, though it may work in some specific setups

For common LSPs, especially permissionless ones, I think this would be quite complex and require a lot of trust. To simplify, the delegator here is usually a set of smart contracts + committee (oracles) for data that is difficult to obtain onchain. There is no single delegator who can simply keep a secret and hand it over later.

The protocol would need a way to generate and store a key share for each validator, and then pass it to the node operator only after the first deposit is final. Maybe the generation part can be solved with cryptography without adding more trust. But for the second part, someone still has to keep the share and release it at the right time.

So this may work in some setups, but for permissionless delegated staking it mostly moves the problem into trusted offchain key custody
